author: Peter Rubinstein
title: Los Angeles police searching for 5-year-old girl and father after mother found slain - NewsBreak
text:
By Peter Rubinstein ,
41 minutes ago A Los Angeles father accused of kidnapping his 5-year-old daughter after killing her mother was reportedly spotted near the U.S.-Mexico border on Wednesday amid an ongoing Amber Alert.
Surveillance footage from a San Ysidro parking garage obtained by NBC Los Angeles appeared to show Ruben Fregoso, 40, and his daughter Daleyza.
The pair had last been seen around 4 a.m. on Sunday in central Los Angeles, according to the Amber Alert issued on Monday.

The Los Angeles Police Department said Fregoso fled from the scene of his wife's possible murder in West Adams with the couple's daughter.
Investigators said Fregoso had made statements indicating he intended to leave the country.
Authorities did not identify the woman, but said a preliminary investigation determined that she died as a result of violence.
The man captured in the surveillance footage on Wednesday was carrying a suitcase and holding the hand of a little girl, NBC reported .
The man was wearing a black vest, ripped jeans and a black hat, and the child was wearing a light blue shirt and sweatpants, the outlet reported.
The California Highway Patrol had said earlier in the week that Fregoso was traveling in a white 2019 Land Rover Discovery.
"Daleyza Fregoso was abducted by Ruben Fregoso and they are believed to be in a white 2019 Land Rover Discovery," the Amber Alert issued by CHP said.
That description matched a vehicle seen in the San Ysidro Point of Entry parking garage, CHP later said. But neither Fregoso nor his daughter were seen at that time.
The alert described Fregoso as standing approximately 5-foot-9 and weighing around 200 pounds. He was said to have black hair and brown eyes.

Daleyza was described as 3 feet tall and weighing 45 pounds, also with black hair and brown eyes.
Authorities requested that anyone with information on the pair's whereabouts call Los Angeles police at (323) 786-5100.
